column1: # Baseline runs: what each module looked like BEFORE any formal-driven fix,
# measured with TODAY's harness.
# Method, four lines, nothing to remember:
#   W=$(mktemp -d) && git worktree add $W --detach <baseline> && cd $W
#   git checkout <harness> -- formal/        # today's harness onto the old RTL
#   git cherry-pick --no-commit <enabling...>   # in the order this table lists
#   formal/run.sh <config>                   # BRAM: baseline/<config>
# Cherry-pick ONLY the named commits, in order. Never hand-edit: an assembled
# state that never existed invalidates the measurement.
# THE BRAM CONFIGS LIVE IN A SUBFOLDER. formal/{bind,config}/baseline/ holds
# black-box-only variants, invoked as `formal/run.sh baseline/bram_tree_baseline`.
# Its outdir is mkdir -p, so artifacts land away from the main suite, and the
# subfolder is also why `run.sh --all` still sees exactly 13 configs: its glob
# is not recursive. Keeping variant families in a subfolder is what stops them
# contaminating that count.
# NOTE ON LABELLING: a red row is a SHORTCOMING, not necessarily a defect. Some
# are contract questions where the disposition was containment, not repair. The
# manifest records what the run showed and the disposition separately.
# BASELINE is the last commit before the first formal-driven RTL fix. Every
# module already carries the uniform six-port interface.
# HONESTY CAVEAT: this is NOT "the design as originally written".
# The modules once exposed o_full/o_empty before the uniform interface arrived
# which is the formal effort's own work. The claim this table supports is "the design
# as it stood when verification began, once a common interface existed".
# enabling: comma-separated commits, IN CHERRY-PICK ORDER. "-" means none.
# whitebox: whether the aux addenda can bind at baseline at all. BLACK-BOX ONLY IS
#   A DELIBERATE SCOPE DECISION for this table. Where the aux happens to bind
#   (the register family) it is included because it costs nothing; where it cannot
#   (the BRAM modules, whose aux watches signals the fixes created) the row says so.
# ENABLING COMMITS come in three kinds, and the write-up should distinguish them:
#   infrastructure  - parameterisation so the proof can be sized
#   measurability   - elaboration and multiple-driver fixes: each is ITSELF a
#                     finding in its own right
#   unblocking      - a finding fixed to make OTHER findings visible. A row
#                     carrying this is no longer "the baseline"; it is the
#                     baseline after the blocking defect was cleared. Label it.
# COLUMN POSITIONS ARE ALIGNED WITH mutations/SWEEP.tsv ON PURPOSE: field 1 is the
# CLI key, field 5 is the ref --replay rebuilds at, field 7 is the machine-checked
# expectation, field 8 is prose. That alignment is what lets regress.sh share its
# dispatch, control runs, drift warning and verdict parsing across both manifests
# instead of growing a second slightly-different copy of them.
# ref (field 5) MEANS SOMETHING DIFFERENT PER MANIFEST, and this is the one place
# the two modes diverge:
#   SWEEP    the commit the worktree is CHECKED OUT at   (the design moved)
#   BASELINE the commit formal/ is OVERLAID from         (the instrument moved)
# In baseline mode the checkout is ALWAYS pinned to the baseline commit in field 3.
# If it ever follows field 5 instead, the row silently measures TODAY's RTL while
# claiming to measure the pre-verification design: it runs, it looks plausible,
# and it is silently wrong.
# expect vocabulary (same as SWEEP, plus one extension):
#   clean                    0 cex and 0 unreachable covers; a verdict block MUST exist
#   cex:a,b,c                ALL named leaves must fire, not "at least one"
#   cover-unreachable:<n>    vacuity, pinned to a count
# WHY cex TAKES A LIST HERE. A baseline row's whole value is the BREADTH of what
# the harness still sees. Pinning one leaf would let systolic_array quietly drop
# from five counterexamples to one and still report CAUGHT, which is precisely the
# weakened-spec case this table exists to detect.
#row
